tagline: Over the Divide and back again, on the racers' Inner Loop.
intro: Out of Silver City, a silver camp laid out in the summer of 1870, the loop climbs north through Pinos Altos into the Gila National Forest and crosses the forested Continental Divide, then crosses it again. It comes down by Mimbres, swings back west past the open-pit copper mine at Santa Rita, and returns by way of Fort Bayard, 93 miles around. Bicycle racers know it as the Inner Loop, the course of the Tour of the Gila.
The Grant County sheriff arrested Billy the Kid twice for theft, back when he went by Henry Antrim, and later called him a likeable kid. His mother is buried in the town cemetery.

moments.title: Pinos Altos
moments.text: Gold in 1860 made a town of about 9,000 by the 1880s. It was named for its tall pines, which came down as the town went up.

moments.title: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument
moments.text: Forty-five miles up NM 15 from Silver City, the Mogollon people built rooms into five cliff alcoves above Cliff Dweller Canyon and linked them one to the next.

moments.title: Chino Mine
moments.text: Apaches, Spaniards, Mexicans and Americans have all taken copper from this ground at Santa Rita. The open pit was begun in 1910, and the town around it is a ghost town.
